title: helm(private): validate and tighten values schema + init hooks refactor
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Context: The Helm chart for Redwood Private has accumulated permissive values and duplicated init-hook logic. This leads to silent misconfigurations during upgrades and makes rollback behavior brittle in air-gapped/private installs.

This PR tightens the values schema (adds v3 validator), centralizes init/register hooks into a single templated job with clearer lifecycle annotations, and introduces explicit upgrade/rollback compatibility metadata for the private installer. The goal is to reduce failed upgrades caused by unexpected typed values and to make init cleanup deterministic for on-prem clusters.

What I changed (high-level):
- Add charts/redwood-private/values.schema.json (v3). Schema includes explicit types, allowed enums for network.mode, kms.backend, and shaped constraints for persistence sizes.
- Validate helm template rendering during CI against a small matrix of values (k8s 1.25/1.26) to catch schema drift.
- Refactor charts/redwood-private/templates/init-job.yaml into templates/_init-hooks.tpl and call from a single template to avoid duplicated lifecycle hooks.
- Make init job idempotent: it now checks for pre-existing resources and records a lock ConfigMap with annotated generation to support safe retries.
- Add upgrade/rollback compatibility notes in charts/redwood-private/README.md with recommended migration steps for volumes and KMS providers.
- Add helm tests (basic smoke) and a unit test harness for schema validation under charts/test/values-matrix/

Testing and verification:
- Local helm lint + schema validation run against the provided sample values matrix.
- CI ran full chart tests (unit + smoke + render) across the values matrix. One integration test initially failed due to an ordering issue; fixed by making the init job wait for the DB PVC to be bound.

Upgrade notes:
- Non-breaking: If you rely on permissive types (e.g. passing strings where we now expect ints) the chart will reject values; please run the provided schema-checker (./tools/validate-values) before upgrading.
- For clusters using the legacy kms.provider:aws option, follow the README migration steps to switch to kms.backend: "awskms" and update provider-specific config.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add/validate values.schema.json
- [x] Refactor init hooks into templates/_init-hooks.tpl
- [x] Add idempotency/lock for init job
- [x] Add smoke helm tests and CI matrix
- [x] Update README with upgrade guidance

Related: ENG-1384 (values schema consolidation), ENG-1420 (private installer rollback improvements).

review_conversation: Marco Reyes (reviewer): Overall looks good. Two asks: (1) can we keep a short migration script for legacy kms.provider to kms.backend mapping? (2) please add a schema version in README so installers can detect incompatible upgrades.
Evelyn Park (author): Added migration notes in README and included a small mapping helper in tools/validate-values. Also added chart annotation 'valuesSchemaVersion: 3' in Chart.yaml.

Priya Natarajan (reviewer): The init job locking is reasonable but needs a short timeout to avoid stuck upgrades if the lock ConfigMap gets orphaned. Suggest adding an annotation-based TTL and a controller will clean up.
Requested change: add TTL annotation and document fallback steps.

Evelyn Park (author): Implemented TTL annotation on the lock ConfigMap and added a note in README with kubectl commands to remove stale locks. Also added a unit test simulating stale lock removal behavior.
Jordan Li (approver): Verified helm template render for sample matrices and smoke tests. Approving pending CI green. +1 from infra for the locking semantics.
CI Bot: One integration job failed on first run (helm-render: ordering error). Re-ran and all checks passed.
merge_notes: Squashed 6 commits into Chart release changes. Backported a small patch to release/2025-11 branch in follow-up PR.
release_notes: Tighten values schema for Redwood Private Helm chart, centralize init hooks, and add idempotent init lock to improve upgrade/rollback reliability. Operators should run tools/validate-values against their current values before upgrading.
